subject: Film & Cinema
title: Italian Neorealism: Truth in Rubble
description: A quick, practical guide to Italian Neorealism: Truth in Rubble.

hook.text: Italy lay in ruins after WWII. Its filmmakers pointed cameras at the rubble and shot.

buildup.text: Real locations, non-professional actors, and stories of poverty replaced studio escapism.

discovery.text: Bicycle Thieves followed a desperate father — no heroes, no villains, just survival.

twist.text: The Italian government tried to suppress these films, embarrassed by the poverty shown.

climax.text: Neorealism inspired every independent and social-realist film movement that followed.

punchline.text: The cheapest films told the truest stories.

quiz.question: Why did Italian Neorealist filmmakers use real locations and non-actors?
options: Studios were destroyed, and they wanted authentic portrayals of poverty
